message.reasoning_content:
We need to determine crimes. Facts: They forced victim to sign a debt note under duress, took his gold necklace as collateral, then transferred it to another person for cash, etc. This is extortion (敲诈勒索罪) and possibly robbery (抢劫罪) or theft? They used threats and force to obtain property. They also made a false debt note, maybe fraud (诈骗罪) but they used intimidation, so extortion. Also they dealt with stolen property? They received gold necklace that was taken under duress, then transferred to another for cash. Could be "非法占有他人财物罪"? But Chinese criminal law: Extortion (敲诈勒索罪) is obtaining property by threatening to expose secrets or other means. Here they used threats of violence to force victim to give money and necklace. That's robbery (抢劫罪) - taking property by force or threat of immediate violence. They forced victim in taxi, threatened, took necklace. That's robbery. Also they made a false debt note, maybe fraud (诈骗罪) but the note was signed under duress, not deception. So main crime: robbery. Also "非法拘禁"? They held him in taxi? They forced him to sign note, but not confinement. Could be "敲诈勒索罪" as they demanded money and got 9000 via false collateral arrangement. However robbery includes taking property by force. They also used intimidation to get a debt note and then used that to get cash from third party. That could be "诈骗罪" because they deceived third party (闫) about the necklace being collateral? Actually they told him they could get 10000 cash, gave him necklace, he gave cash. That's a legitimate transaction? They gave necklace as collateral, got cash. Not fraud. So likely robbery.

Also "聚众斗殴" is mentioned but not part of this case. The defendant had prior conviction for that but not relevant.

Thus list: 抢劫. Possibly also "非法占有他人财物罪" but that's generic theft. In Chinese law, robbery is separate. So answer: [罪名]抢劫<eoa>

Check correction rules: list statutory offense name without “罪”. So just "抢劫". If multiple, separate with semicolons. Only one.
